# Section-valued fields generated by cyclic fibration

## Successor rule

Start with a record type E and fields ell:E->L, s:E->A, t:E->B.
Choose one field p:E->X according to the label/from/to schedule. Define

\[
F(x)=\sum_{e:E}(p(e)=x),\qquad S=\prod_{x:X}F(x).
\]

Promote the selected field type X to S. Define successor rows and evaluation by

\[
E^+=\sum_{\sigma:S}X,\qquad
\operatorname{ev}(\sigma,x)=\operatorname{pr}_1(\sigma(x)).
\]

The selected new field sends (sigma,x) to sigma. Each unselected field h
becomes h composed with ev. Keep x as the old selected-key provenance; the
membership path retained in sigma(x) proves p(ev(sigma,x))=x.

This is an explicit section-to-field rule. It uses the existing homotopy-fiber
and section constructors, with a newly specified successor row type. It is
not the retained-total recurrence T_k from label-from-to-fibration-tower.md.
In particular the old selected field is recovered from provenance, not from
the new section-valued field alone.

## Three steps in HoTT notation

Set E0=E, L0=L, A0=A, B0=B. First promote label:

\[
L_1=\prod_{l:L_0}\sum_{e:E_0}(\ell_0(e)=l),
\qquad E_1=\sum_{\lambda:L_1}L_0.
\]

Read source and target of E1 by evaluation in E0. Next promote source:

\[
A_1=\prod_{a:A_0}\sum_{e:E_1}(s_1(e)=a),
\qquad E_2=\sum_{\alpha:A_1}A_0.
\]

Read label and target of E2 by evaluation in E1. Next promote target:

\[
B_1=\prod_{b:B_0}\sum_{e:E_2}(t_2(e)=b),
\qquad E_3=\sum_{\beta:B_1}B_0.
\]

The next three steps repeat on E3 with field types (L1,A1,B1), producing
(L2,A2,B2). All families are formed from the CURRENT record type and maps.

## Rung table with explicit phase convention

Rung12 is the initial record presentation. The selected field on 12->11 is
label. Every subsequent transition advances the selector. Thus:

| Rung | Record type | Label field | From field | To field |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 12 | E0 | L0 | A0 | B0 |
| 11 | E1 | L1 | A0 | B0 |
| 10 | E2 | L1 | A1 | B0 |
| 9 | E3 | L1 | A1 | B1 |
| 8 | E4 | L2 | A1 | B1 |
| 7 | E5 | L2 | A2 | B1 |
| 6 | E6 | L2 | A2 | B2 |
| 5 | E7 | L3 | A2 | B2 |
| 4 | E8 | L3 | A3 | B2 |

This table describes fixed column names. To match the proposed schematic in
which the first transition promotes the displayed target, one must either start
the selector at target, or explicitly rotate the displayed field roles. The
label-first rule with fixed field roles promotes the label first. No implicit
column renaming or gauge identification is used here.

## Recovery and growth

Evaluation is a well-typed map E+ -> E. It need not be an equivalence. For finite
sets, with fiber sizes n_x:

    number of sections = product_x n_x,
    number of successor rows = |X| * product_x n_x,
    preimages of an old row over x = product_(y different from x) n_y.

An empty fiber can remove all sections even when old rows exist. Singleton
fibers give bijective evaluation in the finite set model. Nontrivial fibers
can create multiple section contexts for the same old row. Two fibers of size2
give four sections and eight evaluation rows from four original rows.

Consequently section promotion changes the available records, while retained
original rows can still be stored separately for guaranteed recovery. The
rule creates recursively dependent endpoint/label types; it does not force a
universal row-count doubling or derive U(1), SU(2), SU(3).

## Verification

    python research/nima/checkers/check_section_endpoint_promotion.py

The finite checker tests all three field choices on 147 endpoint-unique tables:
441 cases. It checks field preservation through evaluation, membership, section
cardinalities, and old-row multiplicities. Among these cases 100 erase a nonempty
input because of empty fibers, and 144 expand row count. An eight-transition
singleton-fiber example verifies iteration and row reconstruction through the
whole schedule. The formulas above define the HoTT construction; no new Agda
compilation or homotopy-level equivalence proof is claimed for this successor.
